title: Gate canonical source traceability and issue-evidence coverage in CI
stage: V2 foundation (CI guard over the existing canonical records)
body:
## Why / user outcome
Prevent the source-to-requirement-to-design/proposal/test/issue evidence chain from silently drifting as source text, canonical mappings, proposal packets, or publication receipts change. This is a CI regression guard over existing traceability artifacts—not a second inventory or a new requirements source.

## Current repository evidence
`inventory/statements.jsonl` is the generated canonical, source-excerpted inventory built from existing source shards by `inventory/build_canonical_inventory.py`; `inventory/README.md` says not to claim atomic completeness. `traceability/mapping.json` is the reviewed bridge, currently `version:1, rows:[]` at this checkout. `tools/build_traceability.py` already validates the shared proposal array fields, mapping schema, duplicates, proposal references, final source excerpt hashes, unmapped normative records and final numeric issue receipts. Its CLI has no output side effect unless `--output-dir` is passed. It does not yet gate CI, compare canonical source digests/ranges against all current source bytes, reject mapping source IDs absent from canonical inventory, or enforce complete issue-packet test/evidence fields. `.github/workflows/scripts-test.yml` currently has no traceability regression step.

## Scope and affected files/interfaces
Extend and test the existing path only: `tools/build_traceability.py`, `inventory/build_canonical_inventory.py` (a read-only `--check`/comparison mode if needed), new focused tests/fixtures under `tools/`, `traceability/README.md`, and a step in `.github/workflows/scripts-test.yml`. Consume the generated `inventory/statements.jsonl`, existing source shards, reviewed `traceability/mapping.json`, current proposal arrays under their existing directories, and the sanctioned publication-receipt input. Do not create a second canonical inventory, duplicate requirement registry, proposal manifest, issue-number database, or test-status source of truth. Do not rewrite or republish the requirement corpus in this issue.

## Measurable acceptance
1. CI proves `inventory/statements.jsonl` is reproducible from the existing shards in check-only mode; check-only does not rewrite the generated file or any source shard.
2. Every canonical row's source ID is unique; every mapped source ID resolves to one canonical row; every source path/range is in bounds; full-source SHA-256 and exact inclusive excerpt/hash match the checked-in canonical record.
3. Every mapped proposal ID resolves to exactly one current shared-schema proposal array entry; mapping IDs and receipt proposal IDs cannot be unknown, duplicate, or contradictory.
4. Final traceability mode fails on every unmapped normative source row, missing proposal/test-oracle/evidence field, invalid disposition/reason, missing numeric publication receipt, or proposal body that omits coordinator §4.2 required issue sections (user outcome, current evidence, scope, measurable acceptance, security/environment, tests/oracle, priority/urgency, lifecycle/stage/size, rollback/recovery, open decisions).
5. A valid fixture with all required dispositions and receipts produces deterministic summary/rows; absent publication receipts before issue publication are reported as incomplete, never falsely complete.
6. `.github/workflows/scripts-test.yml` invokes the check without network, provider, GitHub, credential, CA-key, DNS, trust, or production access; default validation writes no files.
7. Existing proposal arrays are discovered from the established `proposals/` and `designs/proposals/` directories (or passed explicitly by the existing tool); adding a proposal file cannot be silently omitted from the check. No duplicate manifest is introduced.

## Negative tests and oracle
Use compact fixture inventories/source files/mappings/proposal arrays/receipt JSONL and compare exact expected errors and stable output bytes. Required fail fixtures: source file hash changed; line range shortened, shifted, or out of bounds; canonical builder drift; duplicate/unknown stable `source_id`; unknown proposal ID; unmapped normative row in final mode; invalid non-proposal disposition without reason; proposal missing acceptance/test oracle/evidence; missing/conflicting numeric issue receipt; malformed args/unknown flag. Positive oracle: canonical JSONL/CSV/Markdown report byte-equals a checked-in test golden and recomputed SHA-256/excerpt equals source bytes. Error messages must name the failing source/proposal ID and reason. No test may use issue/API live state.

## Security and safe environment
Read-only source and fixture validation. No secrets, production keys, provider vault access, issue creation, queue writes, deployed-service calls, or live operations. Receipt fixtures contain only numeric issue IDs/URLs already published via the authorized process; CI never calls GitHub to create or query issues.

## Dependencies, priority, lifecycle, size, stage
Parent #9156; no other stable proposal-ID prerequisite is known, so `depends_on` is empty. Completion of the reviewed mapping and publication-receipt input is a readiness condition, not an invented proposal dependency. Estimated complexity: Medium (M); V2 foundation; High, intrinsic urgency 600; lifecycle Backlog until those inputs exist, then Ready. Urgency is separate from importance/blocking/stage/dispatch and not queue priority.

## Failure, rollback, recovery
A failed check blocks the CI job with a precise source/proposal ID; it must not modify inventory/mapping/proposal inputs. To recover, correct the authoritative source/mapping/proposal owner and rerun. If the checker rejects a valid edge case, fix the checker and its golden fixture together; never waive an unmapped normative record or silently regenerate reviewed mappings.

## Open decisions
The output location and format of verified numeric issue receipts must follow the sanctioned publisher; this issue must not invent a competing receipt store. Final mode may run as a protected check only after the canonical mapping/receipt set is reviewed.

title: Freeze V1 Fleet CLI and capability-profile compatibility golden corpus
source_ranges: fleet_architecture_spec_v0_3.md §1 lines 56-70, §6.1 lines 277-322, §25.1-25.2 lines 1579-1643, §48.2 V3-S25 and §31 SPEC-OPS-005
stage: V2 foundation (characterize V1; no V1 feature implementation)
body:
## Why / user outcome
Freeze an executable baseline for the currently shipped Fleet CLI, secret output/error contract, and full/serve/connect capability profiles. New design work must distinguish verified V1 behavior from proposed V2+ behavior. This issue adds characterization tests only; it does not implement `cert`, `generate`, or any other new V1 domain.

## Current repository evidence
At pinned census commit `34faffbff26615e313488f6d04705a444342e41e`, `fleet secrets` implements only `get` and `list`: get is broker-first with BWS fallback and intentionally writes the requested value to stdout; list is broker names only and does not fall back to a BWS vault listing. Secrets command codes are 0 success, 2 usage, 3 unresolved/unavailable. The root multicall returns 0 success, 2 usage/unknown, and 69 for compiled/profile/config capability stubs. `fleet-registry` models compiled/profile/effective capabilities; current profiles are full, serve and connect. `DOMAINS` has no `cert`, `pki`, or `generate`. Current tests cover leaf help/line-write behavior in `fleet/src/secrets.rs` and profile nesting in `fleet-registry`, but there is no exact end-to-end V1 stdout/stderr/exit golden matrix in the inspected paths.

## Scope and affected files
Add versioned `v1` golden fixtures and tests under `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet/tests/**` and/or focused unit tests in `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet/src/secrets.rs` and `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-registry/src/lib.rs`; wire the existing variant matrix in `.github/workflows/fleet-rust-tests.yml` only if needed. A private test seam may inject fake broker/BWS sources into command handling, but production resolver order/config/defaults must not change. Do not add commands, capabilities, provider adapters, or a new CLI. Keep the absence of `cert`/`pki`/`generate` as a versioned snapshot of V1, not a permanent prohibition on later domain work.

## API/CLI behavior and measurable acceptance
1. `fleet secrets get <name>` fixture: exact stdout is the requested sentinel plus current line terminator; stderr contains no sentinel; success exit 0. Do not assert that get never prints its result value.
2. `fleet secrets list` fixture: exact broker name-only output, deterministic order, no value, and no BWS inventory fallback. Broker error exits 3 and does not silently enumerate BWS.
3. Secret usage/arity/unknown leaf arguments return 2; unresolved get returns 3; top-level unavailable compiled/profile capability stub returns 69; successful help returns 0.
4. Full/serve/connect snapshots record canonical domains, aliases, subcommands, compiled/profile/effective availability and exit status. Connect is proxy-only; its secret/queue/other unavailable behavior remains stub code 69. Existing registry invariant `connect ⊂ serve ⊂ full` continues to hold.
5. Pinned V1 baseline snapshots show `secrets` offers only `get/list` and no `cert`, `pki`, or `generate` capability at that source revision. Later feature implementation updates a separately versioned snapshot in its owning proposal; this issue does not make future expansion fail forever.
6. All fixtures run hermetically with fake transports/runner and never contact a live broker, BWS, OP, or provider.

## Negative tests and oracle
Use deterministic fake broker responses and a stub BWS runner. Fail if: get output differs byte-for-byte; a secret sentinel appears in stderr/Debug/error; list calls BWS after broker failure; malformed/empty/error resolution returns success; invalid args return a provider error instead of usage 2; `fleet-connect` reports a domain available or dispatches a command not compiled; profile widens compiled capabilities; V1 snapshot advertises cert/pki/generate. Oracle: checked-in versioned stdout/stderr/exit goldens and registry capability sets derived from `full_capabilities`, `serve_capabilities`, `connect_capabilities`; fake invocation log proves no unapproved source call. Preserve expected sentinel on successful get stdout.

## Security and safe environment
Synthetic names/values only. Never invoke a live secrets broker, BWS or other vault; use a stubbed command runner/socket fixture. No CA keys, provider credentials, deployments, DNS/trust changes, or writes.

## Dependencies, priority, lifecycle, size, stage
Parent #9156; no dependencies. Estimated complexity: Small/Medium (S/M); V2 foundation as V1 characterization only; High, intrinsic urgency 600; lifecycle Ready. Do Now/direct dispatch is not inferred. Urgency remains separate from importance/stage and Project/queue priority.

## Failure, rollback, recovery
A changed golden is a compatibility change requiring a versioned baseline update plus an owning implementation/design issue and reviewer explanation. If a test harness requires changing production semantics, stop and retain the V1 implementation; adjust only the test seam. Removing characterization tests is not a rollback for product behavior.

## Open decisions
Decide whether stdout fixtures are captured through a private writer seam or a hermetic subprocess with fake socket/runner. Both must use the exact current V1 CLI entry path and preserve production defaults.
